title: security: rbac v2 - enforce KMS region residency and enhance audit logging
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Enforces KMS region residency constraints for RBAC v2 resources and expands audit logging to include KMS key and residency decisions. No customer-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: customers in regulated regions require strong enforcement that keys and crypto operations remain in their designated cloud region. This PR extends RBAC v2 policy evaluation to enforce KMS region residency constraints and significantly improves audit events so decisions around KMS usage and residency are fully traceable. Design: add a residency check in the RBAC evaluator that consults the KMS residency service and policy predicates, surface decision metadata on audit events (kms_key_id, residency_allowed, residency_reason), and add a lightweight migration to tag existing KMS bindings. Implementation details: implement services/kms/kms_residency.go with a cached check and TTL, update services/rbac/evaluator.go to short-circuit deny when residency mismatch is detected, add audit event fields in services/audit/audit_events.go, add proto changes in api/v1/policy.proto, update docs and add integration/unit tests. Rollout notes: guarded behind feature flag `rbac_v2_kms_residency` and config toggle `kms.enforce_residency` for downstream Dedicated/Private customers; deploy to staging, enable for 10% traffic, monitor audit logs and latency for 24h, then promote. Checklist: - [x] Residency check implementation - [x] Audit events augmented - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Migration script for existing bindings - [x] Docs + changelog - [x] Feature flag gating and config toggle - [x] Security review and threat-model notes Testing: unit and integration tests added for policy evaluator, audit events, and KMS residency cache; staged manual validation with simulated cross-region key access; load test shows <1% median latency increase. Rollback: feature flag flip and quick config revert. References: ENG-4821, SEC-317, SUP-1423.

review_comments: Carlos Mendes (2024-11-04): Question: do we short-circuit before or after other RBAC checks? Short-circuiting earlier prevents unnecessary KMS API calls but may change audit semantics.
Priya Nair (2024-11-04): Reply: We short-circuit at the start of resource-level evaluation to avoid extra work; audit events include the residency_decision so the deny reason is explicit.
Ruth Kim (2024-11-05): Request changes: please add metrics for residency cache hit/miss and TTL evictions so we can tune the TTL in production.
Priya Nair (2024-11-05): Update: added metrics in pkg/telemetry/labels.go and included telemetry report in services/kms; added unit tests for cache behaviour.
Jared O'Neill (2024-11-06): Approval: security review completed, threat model updated, migration script reviewed. Minor request to ensure migration is idempotent.
CI Bot (2024-11-07): e2e flaky on first run, reran successfully.

testing_notes: Added unit tests for policy evaluator and kms residency, added integration test that simulates cross-region key access, manual staging validation done with feature flag enabled for a sample org.
risk_assessment: low: behavioural change only when feature flag and enforce_residency config are enabled. Migration tags are additive and idempotent. Performance impact mitigated by residency cache and telemetry added to monitor hit/miss rates.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy to staging and run full integration suite. 2) Roll to canary/staging cluster with feature flag on. 3) Enable for 10% of production traffic, monitor audit logs and telemetry for 24h. 4) Gradually increase to 100% if no issues. 5) For Dedicated/Private, ship config toggle and clear upgrade notes.
